messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty SEV2 page fired — TLS handshake failures spiking in edge-apac-2 and edge-eu-1. Trigger: LB target health dropping + repeated TLS_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE. 5xx surge reported. auto-cc: #incidents, @maya_oncall_sre, @ben_netops

pagerduty: Incident 88921 created and routed to on-call. Escalation policy: SRE -> NetOps -> ProdEng. Page details: priority=high, symptom=TLS handshake failures, affected services=edge-proxy-hosted-api, observed ~27% error rate in apac.

maya_oncall_sre: ack — I'm on it. Gathering context, will triage region by region.

ben_netops: looking at ALB metrics in APAC now. TargetGroup tg-edge-apac-2 shows ~35% unhealthy with TLS handshake errors in access logs: `TLS_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE` and `client_hello_timeout` spikes. EU shows smaller but noticeable bump. No recent infra deploys logged in apac in last 2h.

alice_prod_eng: any customer-impact details? Carlos, do we have support tickets correlating to these regions?

carlos_support: multiple tickets from EU/APAC customers — mobile clients get 502/504 during embed/stream requests. Earliest reports ~09:01 UTC. I'm tagging affected customers and advising retry; will escalate to account teams once we have root cause.

emily_sre_shift: quick health check: cert rotation ran ~08:45 UTC from CI job for wildcard cert (*.redwood.ai). I see ACM cert ARN arn:aws:acm:apac:123:cert/abcd rotated but ALB in apac still lists the old cert (chain truncated). Could be incomplete chain distribution to regional ALBs.

maya_oncall_sre: copying logs from an edge node (sanitized):
```
[09:02:13] ALB: TLS alert: handshake_failure, remote IP 203.0.113.14, backend=10.0.5.21:443, tls_version=TLSv1.3, cipher=TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
[09:02:16] Backend health check failed: GET /health -> 502
[09:03:02] Error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (missing intermediate chain)
```

ben_netops: that x509 error lines up with an intermediary missing in the cert chain on the ALB. For some reason the new cert import may have omitted the intermediate cert bundle in apac region. AWS ACM sometimes resolves this when you reimport with full chain.

maya_oncall_sre: mitigation plan (quick): 1) Shift traffic away from APAC edge pool to EU/US pools to reduce customer impact. 2) Reimport full cert chain to APAC ALB and reattach. 3) Cycle target registration for tg-edge-apac-2 after cert fix. 4) Monitor errors and rollback any problematic weight changes.

ben_netops: executing weight shift now — moving 60% traffic off edge-apac-2 to edge-us-1 and edge-eu-1 using our traffic-router service. Command run:
```
# internal tool
traffic-router set-weights --region apac --weights "us:0.35,eu:0.65,apac:0.0" --reason "emergency tls mitigation"
```
deploy-bot: traffic-router: weights updated (request id tr-cc3a9). Rolling changes across POPs; expect 30-90s convergence.

carlos_support: customers seeing immediate improvement after retries in many cases. Still tracking a handful of persistent errors.

ben_netops: reimporting cert to ALB in apac with full chain now. Command used (ops run by hand):
```
aws elbv2 remove-listener-certificates --listener-arn arn:aws:elbv2:apac:... --certificates CertificateArn=arn:aws:acm:apac:123:cert/old
aws elbv2 add-listener-certificates --listener-arn arn:aws:elbv2:apac:... --certificates Certificate=\"file://wildcard_redwood_fullchain.pem\"
```
Note: we validated PEM contains intermediate and root.

maya_oncall_sre: after reimport/reattach, performing target group health recheck: toggling deregistration delay and forcing new health checks.

ben_netops: ALB now shows full chain and cert subject CN=*.redwood.ai; health checks passing for majority of targets. Handshake error rates dropping from 35% -> 4% over last 5m.

emily_sre_shift: checks: synthetic probes show success across APAC nodes; customer errors down to baseline. Leaving traffic weights at partial shifted values for 15m for stability, then we'll gradually move back.

maya_oncall_sre: summary so far: root cause = partial cert chain missing on regional ALB after rotation, causing TLS handshake failures for some clients. Contributing factor = rotation job didn't verify chain installation on regional ALBs. Impact = intermittent 5xx/handshake failures for edge-hosted API in APAC and degraded for some EU traffic while weights shifted. Actions taken = traffic weight shift, reimported cert with full chain, cycled target health checks, notified support, monitoring.

alice_prod_eng: any immediate follow-up actions? Who owns postmortem?

maya_oncall_sre: assigning postmortem to @alice_prod_eng. Action items for PM/Pipeline: (1) add cert chain verification to rotation job, (2) add regional post-rotation probe to CI, (3) create runbook step to force full-chain reimport on ALBs, (4) alerting rule change to add x509 handshake failures as a distinct metric.

ben_netops: leaving a note for infra: check automation that pushes certs to ALBs — ensure intermediate bundle is included. Also add a small verification script we can run during rotations.

carlos_support: closing tickets as fixed where customers confirm recovery; leaving some open awaiting customer confirmation.

deploy-bot: incident-bot: auto-note created: rollback not required. Canary/CI cert rotation job flagged for follow-up.

maya_oncall_sre: monitoring window open for 60m. If errors remain above 2% for 10m, we'll reopen paging. For now: resolving pagerduty incident.

pagerduty: Incident 88921 acknowledged and resolved by on-call at 09:45 UTC. Timeline logged.

maya_oncall_sre: final note — I'll write a short timeline for the postmortem and link to this thread. Thanks everyone for quick response. :thumbsup:
